prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t definitively name a single “best” company for everyone — the ideal roofer depends on where in Miami you are, your roof type (shingle, tile, metal, TPO, etc.), whether you’re using insurance, your budget, and your timeline. If you tell me your zip code and roof type I can pull a short list of highly rated local contractors and walk you through vetting them. Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to find and choose the best hurricane‑rated roofing contractor in Miami.

What to ask/verify before hiring
- Florida roofing contractor license (check on FL DBPR).  
- Proof of current general liability and workers’ comp insurance.  
- Manufacturer certifications (e.g., GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum, CertainTeed Select) — these affect warranty eligibility.  
- Experience with Miami‑Dade County and Florida Building Code hurricane requirements.  
- References and recent local projects (ask for addresses so you can inspect).  
- Written, itemized estimate including scope, materials (with brand and model), fastening/nailing schedule, underlayment, flashing and hip/ ridge details.  
- Clear start and completion dates and payment schedule (avoid large upfront payments).  
- Warranty details: manufacturer’s warranty and contractor workmanship warranty (length and what’s covered).  
- Will they obtain required permits and arrange inspections? (Contractor should handle permits.)  
- How will they protect landscaping, driveways, and your property during the job?  
- Lien-release policy and final invoicing practices.

Hurricane‑specific items to require
- Use of Miami‑Dade‑approved hurricane‑rated products (NOA/ESR numbers where applicable).  
- Proper wind‑rated fastening patterns and deck attachment (nail type, spacing, and if applicable, ring‑shank screws).  
- Reinforced eaves, hip ends, and ridge details per code.  
- Tie‑downs, straps or clip systems where required for the roof structure.  
- Synthetic hurricane‑rated underlayment and proper flashing at penetrations.  
- Post‑installation wind‑mitigation inspection (to capture insurance discounts).

How to vet contractors quickly
- Check DBPR license and disciplinary history.  
- Read Google and BBB reviews, but weigh recent jobs and responses to complaints.  
- Ask for 3 written bids with comparable scope.  
- Verify manufacturer certifications on the manufacturer’s site (many list certified contractors).  
- Get and call recent homeowner references.  
- Confirm contractor will procure permits and schedule final inspection.

Next steps I can do for you
- If you give me your Miami zip code and roof type (shingle, tile, metal, flat/TPO), I’ll find 3–5 well‑rated local roofing contractors that specialize in hurricane‑rated replacements and give a short pros/cons list for each.  
- I can also provide a sample checklist and questions to give each contractor when you request an estimate.

Tell me your zip code and roof type and I’ll start a tailored shortlist.
